2023-09-25.headline: Entra ID sets 30 September 2025 deadline to leave legacy MFA and SSPR method management
2023-09-25.overview: The period’s only supplied update is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Entra ID. Microsoft says it will retire the ability to manage authentication methods through the legacy Multifactor Authentication (MFA) and Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) policies on 30 September 2025. This is a forward-looking retirement notice, not evidence of an immediate behavior change this week.
2023-09-25.adminImpact: Administrators should plan to migrate methods managed through the legacy MFA and SSPR policies to the converged Authentication methods policy before the deadline. Microsoft describes that policy as the central management point for passwordless, multifactor authentication, and SSPR scenarios. The supplied notice does not include migration steps or technical prerequisites.

keyChanges.title: Management of methods in the legacy policies will be retired
keyChanges.detail: On 30 September 2025, Entra ID will no longer support managing authentication methods in the legacy MFA and SSPR policies. The notice specifically describes retirement of management in those policies; it does not say that the authentication methods themselves will be removed on that date.

2023-12-04.headline: Entra ID FIDO2 registration may offer passkey creation on another device
2023-12-04.overview: The week contains one Entra ID Message Center notice. It describes a changed FIDO2 security key registration experience in which users may receive an operating system- or browser-generated prompt to create a passkey on another device, such as a phone or tablet; some users may see a QR code for that flow. The notice does not establish a preview or general-availability milestone, a policy change, or a required administrator action.
2023-12-04.adminImpact: The concrete impact is to the user experience during FIDO2 registration. Administrators and support teams should be aware that a passkey-on-another-device prompt or QR code may be expected. The supplied evidence identifies no configuration change, migration, retirement, or mandatory action.

keyChanges.title: Alternate-device passkey prompts can appear during FIDO2 registration
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID users registering a FIDO2 security key may see a prompt generated by their operating system or browser to create a passkey on another device, including a phone or tablet. In some cases, a QR code facilitates the option. This is a registration-experience change, not evidence of a separate product launch or availability announcement.

2024-01-22.headline: India-specific removal of MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp is the only Entra ID change recorded
2024-01-22.overview: For the week of 22 January 2024, the supplied data records one Entra ID item: a 26 January Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about removing MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp in India. There are no recorded new, updated, or removed feature or documentation items, and the notice is a service-change communication rather than a feature launch or preview.
2024-01-22.adminImpact: Organizations without users in India can safely disregard the notice, according to its summary. Organizations with users in India should determine whether they rely on this delivery route. The supplied evidence does not state an effective date, replacement method, or specific migration task.

keyChanges.title: MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp is being removed in India
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Authentication notice describes a regional removal of this MFA delivery capability. It is an operational behavior change, not evidence of general availability, preview, or documentation clarification. No timing or replacement channel is provided in the supplied message.

2024-02-19.headline: Entra ID prepares a device-bound passkey preview, with FIDO2 policy and sign-in changes
2024-02-19.overview: The period’s sole supplied item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about a substantive Entra ID authentication change, not a general-availability announcement or a documentation clarification. Beginning in mid-March 2024, Entra ID is expected to add preview support for device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices alongside existing FIDO2 security-key support. The rollout also changes FIDO2 policy handling and makes the end-user sign-in terminology cover passkeys from all supported device types.
2024-02-19.adminImpact: Administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy to allow the passkey providers they intend to support. They should also expect the Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in option to use new, broader wording. The supplied notice does not state that existing FIDO2 security-key support is being retired or that a migration is required.

keyChanges.title: Device-bound passkeys enter Entra ID as a preview authentication method
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-March 2024, Entra ID will support device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices, in addition to its existing support for FIDO2 security keys. The notice identifies this as a preview; it does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 policy must permit the intended passkey providers
keyChanges.detail: To allow specified passkey providers, administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy. This is the concrete configuration impact of extending supported credentials beyond security keys.

keyChanges.title: The Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in label becomes more inclusive
keyChanges.detail: The end-user option will be renamed to "Face, fingerprint, PIN, or security key." The updated sign-in experience will also use the term "passkey" so the wording covers passkey credentials presented from security keys, computers, and mobile devices.

2024-03-04.headline: Microsoft 365 Admin Center user-consent setting to be retired in early April
2024-03-04.overview: The only reported Entra ID change for the week is the retirement of the “User consent to Apps” setting in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center. This changes where the tenant-wide user consent policy is managed, not the existing policy itself.
2024-03-04.adminImpact: No preparation is required. Existing settings will remain unchanged, but administrators will no longer be able to view or edit the policy in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center after the retirement. Use the user consent settings in the Entra portal instead.

keyChanges.title: Retirement of the Microsoft 365 Admin Center consent setting
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft 365 Admin Center experience for “User consent to Apps” will be retired in early April 2024. Management of the tenant-wide user consent policy moves to the corresponding Entra portal experience; the change does not alter existing settings.

2024-03-11.headline: Entra ID: PIM enters Power Platform public preview while Copilot welcome emails expand to external license assignments
2024-03-11.overview: The week of 11 March 2024 contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices for Entra ID. One announces the public preview of Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in the Power Platform admin center, a capability already available since 5 February. The other describes an upcoming late-March through late-April rollout that will send Copilot for Microsoft 365 welcome emails when licenses are assigned through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center. These notices represent a public preview and a change in email behavior—not a reported general-availability release or retirement.
2024-03-11.adminImpact: Power Platform administrators should treat the PIM integration as preview functionality. Organizations that assign Copilot for Microsoft 365 licenses through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center can review direct-communication preferences ahead of the rollout. The notice says organizations can adjust preferences in the Microsoft 365 admin center, while individual users can change their own settings through security and privacy controls; it identifies no required migration.

keyChanges.title: Entra PIM is in public preview in the Power Platform admin center
keyChanges.detail: The 13 March notice announces public preview availability of Entra Privileged Identity Management within the Power Platform admin center; the capability was made available on 5 February 2024. Microsoft describes PIM as providing management, control, and monitoring of access to important organizational resources. The supplied notice does not claim general availability or specify additional requirements.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Power Platform admin center

keyChanges.title: Copilot welcome emails will cover licenses assigned outside the Microsoft 365 admin center
keyChanges.detail: PowerShell and the Microsoft Entra admin center will support Copilot for Microsoft 365 welcome emails when licenses are assigned through methods other than the Microsoft 365 admin center. The rollout is scheduled to begin in late March 2024 and finish in late April 2024. End users will automatically receive the email when direct communications from Microsoft are enabled, and organizations or users can change the applicable communication preferences.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Microsoft Entra admin center / PowerShell

2024-03-18.headline: Entra ID is moving Teams app consent to new resource-specific controls while retiring legacy RSC interfaces
2024-03-18.overview: The period’s only supplied item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice describing a service rollout and retirement, not a documentation clarification. Entra ID and Microsoft Teams are introducing teams- and chat-specific resource-specific consent settings for apps using Chat RSC and Team RSC. The notice does not identify the change as preview or generally available.
2024-03-18.adminImpact: The change began taking effect on March 7, 2024, with rollout to all tenants scheduled to complete by April 14, 2024. Administrators whose processes or tooling depend on the existing Group owner consent settings or API, or the existing Chat RSC API, need to account for their retirement. The new settings are managed through Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets, and Teams-level administrators can manage them independently.

keyChanges.title: New consent controls apply to Teams and chat resources
keyChanges.detail: Resource-specific consent settings are being introduced for apps in Microsoft Teams, covering Chat RSC and Team RSC. Microsoft describes the change as intended to enhance secure app adoption, but supplies no further security requirements or configuration details.

keyChanges.title: Legacy consent settings and APIs are retiring
keyChanges.detail: The existing Group owner consent settings and API, together with the existing Chat RSC API, will be retired as part of this update. This creates a compatibility and administration impact for tenants or automation that still depend on those interfaces.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID — Group owner consent and Chat RSC

keyChanges.title: Administration shifts to Microsoft Graph PowerShell during a staged rollout
keyChanges.detail: The new teams-specific consent settings are managed using Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets. Teams-level admins can manage them independently; the notice says the rollout started taking effect on March 7 and will be complete across tenants by April 14, 2024.

2024-04-29.headline: Dataverse user cleanup for Microsoft Entra identities enters public preview
2024-04-29.overview: The only supplied Entra-related change for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement for a Microsoft Entra ID–related Dataverse capability. The feature is identified as a Public Preview launching 1 May 2024; it is not described as generally available or as a retirement.
2024-04-29.adminImpact: Administrators responsible for Dataverse environments may gain the ability to delete users in a disabled status, including delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Microsoft cites privacy and regulatory requirements and storage reduction as the intended benefits. The evidence does not state that action is mandatory or provide rollout, configuration, eligibility, or automation details.

keyChanges.title: Public Preview of deleting disabled Dataverse users
keyChanges.detail: The announcement covers delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Its summary describes the capability as deleting users with a disabled status from Dataverse environments. Microsoft positions this as a way to support privacy and regulatory obligations and free storage; no evidence is supplied about the deletion workflow or required administrator steps.

2024-05-13.headline: Week of 13 May: replace Workload ID symmetric keys by 15 June; passkey support begins rolling out
2024-05-13.overview: The supplied period contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices, with no documented Entra content additions, updates, or removals. The most consequential change is the planned disablement of symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals. Separately, Entra ID is beginning a staged authentication-strength improvement for device-stored passkeys.
2024-05-13.adminImpact: Organizations using symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals must replace them with asymmetric keys by 15 June 2024 to avoid authentication failures. No preparation is required for the Entra ID passkey rollout, although administrators may update relevant user documentation to reflect the new registration options.

keyChanges.title: Workload ID will disable symmetric keys for first-party application service principals
keyChanges.detail: This Microsoft 365 Message Center major update describes a security-driven authentication behavior change. Organizations must switch from symmetric to asymmetric keys by 15 June 2024; otherwise, affected authentication attempts may fail.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID authentication strength is being improved to support device-stored passkeys
keyChanges.detail: The rollout is scheduled to begin in mid-May 2024 and complete by early August 2024. Users will see new passkey registration options in My Security Info. The notice says no administrator preparation is needed; updating relevant documentation is optional.

2024-05-20.headline: Entra PIM is generally available for time-bound Dynamics 365 and Power Platform tenant admin roles
2024-05-20.overview: The week contained one Entra ID Message Center announcement. Microsoft announced general availability, beginning May 23, 2024, of managing admin roles for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform through Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM). No documentation additions, updates, or removals were supplied.
2024-05-20.adminImpact: Administrators can use Microsoft Entra PIM to assign tenant admin roles for a defined period in Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform. The supplied announcement does not identify additional prerequisites, migration work, or configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: General availability of Entra PIM role management for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform
keyChanges.detail: This is a general availability change—not a preview or documentation clarification. Beginning May 23, 2024, Microsoft Entra PIM supports assigning tenant admin roles for these workloads for a certain time period. The announcement was published in the Microsoft 365 Message Center on May 24.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Privileged Identity Management

2024-07-01.headline: Entra ID Conditional Access Insider Risk condition reaches general availability
2024-07-01.overview: The period’s sole substantive update is the general availability of Microsoft Entra’s Insider Risk condition in Conditional Access. The capability uses insider risk signals from Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection so organizations can enforce Conditional Access actions according to user risk levels. Rollout begins in early July 2024 and is expected to complete by early August 2024.
2024-07-01.adminImpact: Use of the capability requires an Entra ID P2 license and Adaptive Protection to be enabled. Eligible organizations can configure Conditional Access policies that respond to the resulting insider-risk signals; tenants may receive the capability during the stated rollout window.

keyChanges.title: Insider Risk condition is now generally available in Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: This moves the condition from its prior status into general availability and adds insider-risk signals from Adaptive Protection as inputs for Conditional Access policy decisions. The available enforcement behavior is based on user risk levels, rather than only the existing Conditional Access conditions described in the evidence.

keyChanges.title: Prerequisites and rollout are explicit
keyChanges.detail: Organizations need both an Entra ID P2 license and enabled Adaptive Protection to use the feature. Microsoft’s message says rollout starts in early July 2024 and completes by early August 2024, so availability may arrive during that window rather than simultaneously for every tenant.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection

2024-07-08.headline: Azure AD Graph retirement is the clearest lifecycle signal in a sparse Entra week
2024-07-08.overview: The supplied period contains one Microsoft 365 Message Center item, posted 12 July, summarizing June 2024 Microsoft Entra updates. It flags Azure AD Graph retirement, Entra ID releases described as generally available, Apple-device security enhancements, and Entra ID updates affecting older Windows builds. No new, updated, or removed documentation items were supplied, and the record does not include the detail needed to establish feature names, dates, affected versions, or required actions.
2024-07-08.adminImpact: Azure AD Graph retirement is the most consequential item to validate in the underlying Message Center detail, but this record does not support a migration deadline or specific tenant action. The GA, Apple, and Windows references likewise lack enough detail to assess rollout, configuration, or compatibility impact. The period provides no evidence of an ordinary documentation clarification.

keyChanges.title: Azure AD Graph retirement called out
keyChanges.detail: The June 2024 roundup identifies Azure AD Graph Retirement. This is a capability-lifecycle change rather than a documentation update; the supplied message gives no retirement date, scope, migration guidance, or affected workload details.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD Graph

keyChanges.title: Entra ID general availability releases
keyChanges.detail: The message explicitly describes June releases for Entra ID as generally available. It does not name the releases, so no feature-level behavior, eligibility, or administrator step can be stated from the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: Security enhancements for Apple devices
keyChanges.detail: The roundup says that security enhancements for Apple devices were included. It does not identify the Apple platforms, controls, rollout behavior, or configuration changes, so their administrative impact cannot be determined.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID updates affecting older Windows builds
keyChanges.detail: The summary flags Entra ID updates affecting old Windows builds. No build numbers or description of the change are provided, so the evidence does not establish whether this is a support, compatibility, or behavior change.

2024-07-29.headline: Entitlement Management will prevent privileged administrators from bypassing access package approvals
2024-07-29.overview: Starting August 26, 2024, Entitlement Management will enforce access package policy approval settings for Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators. The supplied period contains a single Message Center notice describing this behavior change; it does not report a new feature launch, preview, retirement, or documentation update.
2024-07-29.adminImpact: No action is required from organizations because Microsoft says the change is automatic. Administrators should expect the affected privileged roles to be subject to the approval requirements configured in access package policies rather than being able to bypass them.

keyChanges.title: Approval enforcement extends to Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators
keyChanges.detail: Changes to Entitlement Management will prevent these two administrator roles from bypassing access package policy approvals. The change takes effect on August 26, 2024 and is described as an automatic update.

2024-08-05.headline: Week of 5 August 2024: Edge mobile Copilot retirement leads several Entra availability rollouts
2024-08-05.overview: The supplied period contains five Microsoft 365 Message Center announcements and no new, updated, or removed documentation items. The most consequential user-facing change is the retirement of Copilot in the Microsoft Edge mobile application for Entra ID users with version 128 in late August. Other substantive announcements move Attacker in the Middle detection in ID Protection, the AD FS application migration wizard, and device-based Conditional Access on Red Hat Enterprise Linux to general availability. A separate Dynamics 365 notice announces availability of a feature for deleting certain Microsoft Entra group users.
2024-08-05.adminImpact: The only explicit communication request is to inform affected users about the Edge mobile Copilot retirement and direct them to the Microsoft 365 mobile app for work or web chat. The ID Protection, AD FS migration wizard, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux Conditional Access announcements each state that no action is required before rollout. The Dynamics 365 notice confirms availability beginning 8 August but does not provide enough detail to infer a required cleanup, configuration change, or deletion workflow.

keyChanges.title: Retirement: Copilot in the Edge mobile application for Entra ID users
keyChanges.detail: Copilot in the Microsoft Edge mobile app will be retired with version 128 in late August 2024 for Entra ID users. No administrator action is required, but Microsoft recommends informing users and directing work users to the Microsoft 365 mobile app or web chat instead.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: Attacker in the Middle detection alert
keyChanges.detail: The Attacker in the Middle detection feature in Microsoft Entra ID Protection is scheduled to reach general availability by late August. The capability is intended to identify compromised user accounts, and the notice says no action is required before rollout.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: AD FS application migration wizard
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Entra ID AD FS application migration wizard provides a guided experience for migrating AD FS relying-party applications. Rollout begins in mid-August and is expected to complete by late August; no administrator action is required before the rollout.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: Device-based Conditional Access on Red Hat Enterprise Linux
keyChanges.detail: Device-based Conditional Access for Microsoft 365 and Azure resources on Red Hat Enterprise Linux is going generally available in mid-to-late August. The stated support includes Entra ID registration, Conditional Access policies, SSO, Intune compliance, and Red Hat RPM packages; no action is required before rollout.

keyChanges.title: Available: Dynamics 365 deletion of certain Microsoft Entra group users
keyChanges.detail: Starting 8 August 2024, Dynamics 365 will have a generally available feature to delete stub, unlicensed, and removed Microsoft Entra group users. The supplied announcement does not describe the trigger, scope, or administrator workflow, so it does not support a more specific operational recommendation.

2024-08-12.headline: Microsoft requires tenant MFA for admin-portal access by 15 October 2024
2024-08-12.overview: The week’s sole supplied change was a Microsoft 365 Message Center Major update for Entra ID Authentication. It is a security-enforcement notice, not a new feature or documentation clarification: tenants must enable MFA to retain administrative access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center.
2024-08-12.adminImpact: Administrators should enable MFA before 15 October 2024. The notice also identifies an option to apply to postpone the enforcement date if necessary; without MFA, administrative access to the listed portals will be restricted.

keyChanges.title: Tenant MFA deadline and access restriction announced
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s 16 August notice says MFA must be enabled for the tenant by 15 October 2024 for access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. It advises setting up MFA early or applying to postpone enforcement where necessary. No other Entra feature, availability change, retirement, or documentation update is supplied for this period.

2024-09-02.headline: Microsoft Entra ID announces public preview of FIDO2 provisioning APIs
2024-09-02.overview: The period’s only supplied Entra change is a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement for new FIDO2 provisioning APIs in public preview. The capability is intended to let organizations pre-provision security keys for users, simplifying onboarding and supporting phishing-resistant authentication. Rollout is scheduled to begin in mid-September 2024 and finish by late September.
2024-09-02.adminImpact: No administrator action is required for the rollout. The announcement does not provide configuration, eligibility, or migration requirements, and the capability should be treated as a public preview rather than a generally available feature.

keyChanges.title: Pre-provisioning of FIDO2 security keys enters public preview
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID is introducing APIs that enable security keys to be provisioned for users before onboarding. This changes the onboarding workflow the preview is designed to support, while the supplied notice does not establish general availability or require administrators to make changes during rollout.

2024-09-09.headline: Tenant MFA action deadline set for 15 October 2024
2024-09-09.overview: The week contains one Microsoft 365 Message Center action for Microsoft Entra ID. Administrators are asked to enable multifactor authentication (MFA) for the tenant by 15 October 2024 to access the Microsoft Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. No supplied evidence indicates a new Entra feature, documentation change, or retirement during this period.
2024-09-09.adminImpact: Review tenant MFA readiness before the deadline. Postponement is possible, but administrators signing in without MFA will be prompted to register for it, which changes the sign-in experience and may affect access to the listed admin centers.

keyChanges.title: MFA becomes an explicit prerequisite for access to key admin centers
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice calls for tenant MFA enablement by 15 October 2024 for access to the Azure, Entra, and Intune admin centers. This is an administrative security action and deadline, not a product launch. If MFA is not enabled, admin sign-in will prompt MFA registration; the notice also states that postponement is available.

2024-10-07.headline: Microsoft Edge Mobile will change the New tab experience for Microsoft Entra ID users
2024-10-07.overview: The week contained one Microsoft 365 Message Center notice and no recorded Entra documentation additions, updates, or removals. The notice concerns Microsoft Edge Mobile rather than a new Entra ID capability: Wallpaper will be enabled by default on the New tab page, and a weather icon will be added. The changes were expected to roll out in early and late October 2024, respectively.
2024-10-07.adminImpact: No administrator action is required before the rollout. Administrators should expect affected Microsoft Entra ID users on Microsoft Edge Mobile to see the updated New tab defaults as the changes arrive.

keyChanges.title: Edge Mobile is changing the default New tab experience
keyChanges.detail: For Microsoft Entra ID users, Wallpaper will be enabled by default, with the wallpaper rollout expected in early October 2024. A weather icon was expected to follow in late October 2024. This is an announced user-experience behavior change, not evidence of a new Entra ID feature or a change to Entra ID administration.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Edge Mobile / Entra ID users

2024-10-14.headline: Entra message flags Azure AD Graph retirement, MFA enforcement and Apple-device security changes—but provides no operational details
2024-10-14.overview: The only supplied signal for the week of 14 October 2024 is a 15 October Microsoft 365 Message Center roundup for Microsoft Entra ID. Its summary says the September 2024 update covered general-availability releases, Azure AD Graph retirement, security enhancements for Apple devices and MFA enforcement. It is a communication pointing administrators to release notes, blog and email details—not a standalone record of a new feature, preview or documentation change made during this week.
2024-10-14.adminImpact: The message supports awareness but not a specific implementation step. The supplied evidence does not identify the affected GA releases, retirement date or migration scope, Apple-device behavior, MFA target population, enforcement schedule or prerequisites. Administrators need the referenced release material to determine whether action is required. No separate new, updated or removed documentation changes are recorded for the period.

keyChanges.detail: The summary says the update included MFA enforcement, but does not specify which users, tenants, authentication flows or policies are covered, nor when enforcement applies. No administrator action can be inferred from this message alone.

keyChanges.title: Security enhancements for Apple devices are called out
keyChanges.detail: The message identifies security work for Apple devices, but supplies no affected capability, platform behavior, rollout status or configuration requirement. The record therefore does not support a more specific assessment of impact.

keyChanges.title: General-availability releases are referenced but not identified
keyChanges.detail: The September roundup says it includes general-availability releases, but names no features or capabilities and provides no dates or availability scope. The reference alone is insufficient to characterize a launch or determine whether administrators need to change configuration.

2024-11-04.headline: Entra ID will reintroduce WhatsApp for MFA OTP delivery in India starting December 2024
2024-11-04.overview: The only supplied change for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update affecting Entra ID. Beginning in December 2024, users in India who have WhatsApp will receive MFA one-time passcodes through WhatsApp, with SMS used as a fallback. Microsoft says the channel will expand to additional countries, but does not specify which ones or when.
2024-11-04.adminImpact: Review whether WhatsApp-based OTP delivery fits the organization’s authentication policy before the rollout. Administrators can disable the feature or direct users toward stronger methods such as Microsoft Authenticator; the supplied notice does not provide configuration steps or a more specific rollout schedule.

keyChanges.title: WhatsApp becomes an MFA OTP delivery channel again
keyChanges.detail: This is a planned service behavior change and regional rollout—not a documentation-only clarification. Entra ID will reintroduce WhatsApp delivery in India from December 2024, with expansion to more countries. Users with WhatsApp will receive the code there, while SMS remains the fallback channel.

2025-01-20.headline: Entra ID is enabling Authenticator passkeys for FIDO2 organizations without key restrictions
2025-01-20.overview: The week of 20 January 2025 contains one substantive item: a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Entra ID Authentication. Starting in late January 2025, organizations with an enabled passkey (FIDO2) policy and no key restrictions will have passkeys available in the Microsoft Authenticator app. The supplied evidence describes an enablement notice, not a documentation change, and does not label the capability as preview or generally available.
2025-01-20.adminImpact: Administrators in the affected configuration should expect users to be able to add an Authenticator passkey through aka.ms/MySecurityInfo, with use enforced by Conditional Access policy. Organizations that do not want this enablement can impose key restrictions. No additional rollout scope or administrative steps are provided.

keyChanges.title: Authenticator passkeys become available under a specific FIDO2 policy configuration
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in late January 2025, passkeys in the Microsoft Authenticator app will be available to organizations that have enabled passkey (FIDO2) policy and have not configured key restrictions. Users can add the passkey through aka.ms/MySecurityInfo, and Conditional Access policy governs enforcement. This is the period’s only supplied change.

2025-02-17.headline: Entra is introducing a dedicated Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
2025-02-17.overview: The week of 17 February contains one reported Entra change: a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement about a new built-in role for Viva Glint. The rollout is expected from late March to early April 2025. No separate Entra documentation updates, retirements, or other product changes are included in the supplied period.
2025-02-17.adminImpact: The role is intended to let administrators manage Viva Glint settings without Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges. Administrators should review the role documentation, assess current role assignments, and communicate the change to affected staff before the rollout.

keyChanges.title: New built-in Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is introducing the role in Microsoft Entra to provide Viva Glint settings management without requiring Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges. This is a planned rollout announcement, not evidence that the role is already generally available; the stated rollout window is late March to early April 2025.

2025-03-03.headline: Microsoft Entra rolls out a People administrator role while ID Protection alerts move to Defender XDR
2025-03-03.overview: The supplied record for the week of 3 March contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices and no documentation additions, updates, or removals. Microsoft Entra is rolling out a new People administrator role, while Entra ID Protection alerts are being removed from Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and integrated into Microsoft Defender XDR.
2025-03-03.adminImpact: The People administrator role is intended to support people-related administration and profile-photo management without requiring high privileges; the notice does not specify assignment steps or label the capability as preview or generally available. For ID Protection, the notice says no administrator action is required, but asks administrators to review their configuration and notify users about the change in alert location.

keyChanges.title: New People administrator role begins rollout
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is introducing a People administrator role based on customer feedback. It allows management of people-related settings and profile photos without requiring high privileges. The stated rollout began in early February 2025 and is expected to complete by late March; the notice describes a rollout but does not establish preview or general-availability status.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection alerts leave Defender for Cloud Apps
keyChanges.detail: Starting 5 March 2025, Microsoft Entra ID Protection alerts are no longer available in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and are integrated into Microsoft Defender XDR. This is a change to where the alerts are surfaced, not an evidence-based statement that ID Protection alerting itself is being retired. The notice says no admin action is required, while recommending configuration review and user notification.

2025-03-10.headline: Entra ID: “Require approved client app” control planned for retirement in March 2026
2025-03-10.overview: The only supplied update for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center reminder that the “Require approved client app” Conditional Access control will be retired in March 2026. Microsoft directs organizations to update affected policies to use the “Require application protection policy” grant control. This is a planned retirement notice, not a new feature, preview, general availability announcement, or evidence that the control has already been removed.
2025-03-10.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access policies that use the retiring control and plan updates to the named replacement before March 2026.
